title: node.py: assert for runtime None check bypassed by -O flag
description:
Line 407 uses assert to check that persistence_revision_anchor is not None when persist_path is set. This assert can be skipped with Python's -O flag, potentially causing a None to be passed to AnnounceStatePersistence.

Location: python/src/lichen/node.py:407
Issue: assert self.persistence_revision_anchor is not None

The API contract (if persist_path is set, persistence_revision_anchor must also be set) is not enforced by explicit validation in __post_init__, only by this assert.

Fix: Replace with explicit ValueError check like:
  if self.persistence_revision_anchor is None:
      raise ValueError('persistence_revision_anchor required when persist_path is set')

Severity: P2 - potential None dereference in production with -O
close_reason: RE-CLOSE (third landing; prior closes were lost to two shared-dolt-store reverts, see bead 64gb): The -O-bypassable assert was replaced with an explicit ValueError in Node.__post_init__ (node.py:363-369), enforced before LinkLayer/AnnounceStatePersistence construction; use-site narrowed with cast. Regression test_node_persist_path_requires_revision_anchor added. Premise note preserved: LinkLayer already raised ValueError for this case (link_layer.py:291-296) so the assert was effectively unreachable — severity overstated, but the contract is now explicit at the Node boundary and immune to -O (verified under python3 -O). Code commits c26c012c2d and 7fdec586ba on beads-worker-5. 3x codereview via reviewer model: correctness PASS, security PASS, edge-cases no findings.
